newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end down as Dow drops, technicals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end down as Dow drops, technicals.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed lower on light, late selling with a drop in the Dow Jones Industrial stock index also mentioned, traders said.
"It was a bearish technical close. After being higher early we closed lower and that's not very encouraging for the bulls," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Traders said the drop in the Dow probably had a mild influence on soybeans and cited nearly ideal crop weather in South America as an ongoing bearish price factor.
"Maybe the Dow break had a little to do with it but not much," Lespinasse said.
The Dow was down over 50 points at midsession and at 1430 CST was down 34 points.
Agronomists said Brazilian soy seedings are overall active but farmers noted the need for more rain to boost prospects.

"Some regions are dry, principally in the west and the center-south, but for the time being there is no great cause for concern," said Otmar Hubner, agronomist at the Parana Staate Agricultural Secretariat.
Soybeans closed four cents per bushel lower to 1/4 higher, with January down two at $6.97. March was down 1-1/4 at $6.91-1/4.
Technicians pointed to the $7.00 per bushel mark in the January as central to the market's performance.
The January contract surged on November 29 to a recent high of $7.18-1/2 per bushel a rally many fundamentalists and technicians labeled "too much too soon."
Export news was generally lackluster and nondescript with exporters noting a tender by Taiwan late this week for 32,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and soybeans, 12,000 corn and 18,000 soybeans.
Cargill Inc sold 1.5 million bushels of March and Refco Inc bought two million January and sold one million January, traders said.
Tenco Inc bear spread two million bushels of March/January, they said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 46,000 contracts, below the 56,576 traded Tuesday, according to the CBOT.
In soybean options, Cargill Investor Services sold 400 March $7.00 calls at 15-1/2 to 16 cvents and Continental Grain sold 400 January $7.00 calls at 8-1/4 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 13,500 contracts, below the 16,358 traded Tuesday.
